nodes.label: Build order (§10)
nodes.rationale: Scaffold → G0 spike → offscreen plumbing → fixture capture → Canvas → Gradescope/PrairieLearn/PrairieTest → normalize+dedupe → store+sync+popup (G2, G3) → notifications → options/overrides/.ics → adapters → report flow/policy/store (G4, G5).

nodes.label: Gate G2 — Recall
nodes.rationale: End-to-end sync on the author's account lists every deadline visible on every source for 3 weeks (100% recall, no phantoms). PASSED on live data.

nodes.label: Gate G3 — Dedupe
nodes.rationale: Auto-merge produces the right groups with ≤2 manual corrections, else tune §5.3. Passed on n=1 merge; the threshold question stays open until G4.

nodes.label: Gate G4 — Beta
nodes.rationale: 10 users across ≥3 majors for a week; zero data-loss bugs, every parse error surfaced, ≥7 of 10 would keep it. Sushi's; cannot start from the agent side.

nodes.label: Report a broken page flow
nodes.rationale: User pastes a URL; the extension fetches it, scrubs PII (emails, the student's name), and offers a download to attach to a GitHub issue. Nothing is sent automatically.

nodes.label: Risk: silent missing deadline
nodes.rationale: Catastrophic if it happens; mitigated by §0 rule 3 (fail loudly), per-source health dots and the G2 recall test.

nodes.label: Title normalization (§5.2)
nodes.rationale: Comparison only, display never altered: lowercase, strip punctuation, synonyms (homework→hw, machine problem→mp), join prefix+number (hw 02→hw2), drop filler tokens, result is a token set.

nodes.label: Review policy
nodes.rationale: Full adversarial review (~20 min, ~1.5M tokens) only for core/dedupe.ts and the sync loop, where G2/G3 risk lives; light or no review for refactors and UI, relying on the mutation-tested suite. Findings whose refuters fail are unverified, not refuted.

nodes.norm_label: defect: source off but its rows still on the calendar

Rows drop in both disabled branches and withoutRows applies it the moment the switch flips; overrides survive. Three tests pinned the defect.

nodes.norm_label: defect: a failed fetch was reported as parse_error

nodes.norm_label: defect: 'couldn't be read' for both parse and network failures

Now 'Gradescope didn't answer' (retryable) vs 'Canvas looks different' (needs a build), with a character budget pinned; actionFor returns a login/retry/open action for every failing state; the pill reads Checking… during a sync, capped by SYNC_SPINNER_CAP_MS because sendMessage does not reject when the worker dies.

nodes.norm_label: defect: the sync took the sum of its sources

nodes.label: Notifications (§7)

nodes.label: Offscreen document (DOM_PARSER)
nodes.rationale: MV3 service workers have no DOMParser. Regex is fragile and a bundled HTML parser adds 100KB+, so chrome.offscreen with reason DOM_PARSER is used. DOMParser documents are inert (no script execution, no resource loading), which is the security property wanted when parsing untrusted HTML.

nodes.label: Service worker architecture (§2)
nodes.rationale: chrome.alarms every 30 min runs runSync: fetch → parse (via offscreen) → normalize → dedupe with overrides → store → notifications; registry refreshed daily.

nodes.label: Sync loop runSync (§6)
nodes.rationale: For each enabled source not in backoff: plan → fetchAll → login check → parseAll via offscreen → replace that source's raw items atomically → mark ok; ParseError → parse_error + backoff, NetworkError → network_error + backoff. Then dedupe, store items, schedule notifications. A failing source never blocks the others.

nodes.label: Check it in the mode Sushi actually uses (dark)
nodes.norm_label: check it in the mode sushi actually uses (dark)
nodes.rationale: Every verification screenshot was light while Sushi's machine is dark. A tint does different work at each end: 5.5% navy on white drops 12/255, 6% pale blue on #1c1c1c lifts 8, and the eye is less sensitive near black — dark tints are roughly double. Measure the composited luminance rather than trusting the alpha.

nodes.label: Sushi's time is the scarce resource
nodes.norm_label: sushi's time is the scarce resource
nodes.rationale: Every browser round-trip is a real interruption. Ask for one action at a time with exact steps and what each answer would prove; exhaust what the repo can answer first; prefer diagnostics that distinguish several hypotheses; when a round-trip is spent on something a log line would have answered, add the log line.

nodes.label: UI rule 1: a popup and the service worker have different consoles
nodes.norm_label: ui rule 1: a popup and the service worker have different consoles

nodes.label: Worker rule 5: log both branches of any decision the user will have to debug
nodes.norm_label: worker rule 5: log both branches of any decision the user will have to debug
nodes.rationale: A silent early return in the registry seed made 'already seeded' and 'the seed never ran' identical in the console, costing two rounds of browser time — the most expensive resource in the project.

nodes.label: §0.5 Chrome only
nodes.rationale: Firefox later; MV3 differences (no offscreen API in Firefox). The parser layer is written so it can move, nothing else is abstracted.

nodes.label: §0.4 Declarative adapters only
nodes.rationale: Course-site adapters are JSON (URLs + CSS selectors + date formats), never code. Manifest V3 forbids remotely loaded code; remote data is fine, so selectors can be fixed without a store re-review.

nodes.label: Remote code: none — adapters are data, not code
nodes.norm_label: remote code: none — adapters are data, not code

nodes.norm_label: daily cookieless fetch of one public file on raw.githubusercontent.com

nodes.label: Remote code: No
nodes.rationale: The daily fetch returns data — CSS selectors, a date format, a timezone, a filter pattern — interpreted by a runner inside the package; no eval, no new Function, no remote script.

nodes.label: Course rename override (overrides.courseNames)
nodes.rationale: The last resort for names no rule can derive. First override storing text the student typed: renameCourse deletes on empty (a blank label would make the course vanish), capped at 60 characters, one resolver for all four surfaces, migrateOverrides and courseLabel refuse empties from older builds. nodes.norm_label: defect: a worker on an older build killed the settings page

nodes.label: Worker rule 8: a message from the worker is data from another build, not a typed object
nodes.norm_label: worker rule 8: a message from the worker is data from another build, not a typed object
nodes.rationale: Chrome reloads an extension page from disk on every open but keeps the running service worker, so the two routinely disagree. Response is a compile-time claim about the sender's build; normalize every field a page dereferences (core/compat.ts), name missing ones on screen, never let a render function reject into a console the user does not have open.

nodes.norm_label: defect: the debounce asked 'how long' instead of 'has anything happened'

The worker now records the last completed navigation per source in storage.session and sourcesToRecheck treats a navigation newer than the last attempt as overriding the window; self-limiting because lastAttemptAt then exceeds the navigation. nodes.rationale: Gradescope and PrairieTest did not sync until the student clicked something and came back. tabs.onUpdated reveals a tab's URL only for hosts already permitted, needs no new permission, fires on every completed navigation, and is gated by sourcesToRecheck. core/origins.ts matches hostnames in full (endsWith would accept evilwww.gradescope.com). nodes.rationale: If a host fails Gate 0 (or Cloudflare blocks extension requests, or a site is client-rendered), inject a content script and fetch from page context; uglier because it needs a tab, so only if needed. Not needed after G0 passed 4/4.

nodes.rationale: Requests from extension contexts to host_permissions hosts carry the user's cookies with credentials: include and are exempt from SameSite. The whole project rests on this.

nodes.rationale: Two-stage plan: dashboard (first term group in DOM order) then each course page. No API; ToS discourages automation, so make about the same requests a student's browser would at ≥15 min intervals. Expired sessions redirect to /login.

nodes.label: needs_login detection
nodes.rationale: A response landing on shibboleth, login.illinois.edu or /login is needs_login, reported with a button that opens the source's login page — never parse_error.

nodes.rationale: plan(ctx) → FetchPlan, parse(doc, page) → RawItem[] which throws ParseError on structural surprise and never returns [] for a page whose structure says items exist, isLoginPage(resp, body).

nodes.norm_label: status = most done of the members

nodes.label: Parser rule 11: never signed in is not session expired, and both are needs_login
nodes.norm_label: parser rule 11: never signed in is not session expired, and both are needs_login
nodes.rationale: A student who has never signed in gets 200 at the unchanged URL with an ordinary title (Gradescope marketing splash, PrairieTest with no cards), so the parser throws parse_error — offering nothing to click in the one case where signing in is the fix. Every hosted source needs a positive signed-out marker. Found 2× on a real beta build.

nodes.norm_label: parser rule 12: a signed-out marker must be absent from the healthy page

nodes.label: Parser rule 13: a per-student URL means a source, not an adapter
nodes.norm_label: parser rule 13: a per-student url means a source, not an adapter

nodes.norm_label: parser rule 2: silent empty is the worst outcome

nodes.norm_label: parser rule 6: match markers exactly and scope them to the smallest element

nodes.norm_label: parser rule 8: login detection needs the http status
